customized_feature_details.name: customized_feature_details
customized_feature_details.note:
FIXED IN THE APP, and the shading was wrong rather than merely ugly. The
fetch buffers half a viewport either side and the packer places every buffered
feature, so a window holding nine genes can carry a stack twenty rows deep whose
bottom rows draw nothing in view. The scrollbar and the edge shadow are two
readouts of one number, and measured over the whole pack they answered 'features
are hidden below' about a track showing all of them -- and offered a scroll
gesture onto blank canvas.

scrollExtentMaxY measures the same on-screen set the fit ladder already
measures, on the same 500ms coarse debounce, so a pan re-measures once it
settles. Fit mode was already narrowed at the source. The DRAWING height is
untouched, so a buffered feature keeps its box and its label and is unreachable
rather than clipped.

Three figures in this pass came back for it; this is the one where nothing was
below the fold at all, and its bottom band is now the same white as the rest of
the track.

desktop-available-genomes.name: desktop-available-genomes
desktop-available-genomes.note: might be on homepage. review-screenshots-web says its unused though ANSWERED, and it was a tooling blind spot plus a real drift bug. IT IS ON THE HOMEPAGE -- src/components/HomePage.astro serves it as the 'Available genomes' picker beside the hub copy. review-screenshots-web could not see that: its docRoots were docs, blog and src/pages and it only walked .md/.mdx, so EVERY image the homepage owns reported zero usages, i.e. read as a deletion candidate while being the most-seen picture on the site. THE SECOND HALF is why the question was worth asking: the homepage was serving a HAND-MADE webp dated Jul 19 against a desktop capture recaptured Aug 1, 26% of pixels disagreeing, and nothing reported it -- the review tooling reads the png, the homepage serves the webp, only the png ever gets recaptured. gen-home-images.ts now derives it from the png (a DERIVED map beside HERO, same rationale its own docstring already gave), so a desktop recapture updates the homepage and --check fails when it does not. Height in the astro corrected 764 -> 763, which is what the capture actually is.

DONE 2026-08-08: `bubbleSpread: 'compress'`, where this drew proportionally. It is a loop because it is one 1,199 bp segment attached at two points a few tens of bp apart, which is what an insertion IS -- but under the proportional law it is drawn 20-70x longer than every other node in the cut (17-73 bp) and the only place the layout can put it is a circle that swallows the drawing. The compress law pulls longest and shortest towards the graph's mean, and the two arms come out as a lens you can see is a bubble. Its cost -- the long node no longer READS as long -- costs nothing here. Also named the other arm: the view already labels the link the four other strains take '1.2 kb deletion', so one arm said what it was and the other said nothing, which is most of 'unclear why it is a loop'. Investigated 2026-08-09 against ~/src/vendor/pangyplot as asked. What pangyplot does is not a layout setting: it runs BubbleGun at INGEST time, stores a nested bubble decomposition, serves `/select` as a graph with each top-level bubble collapsed to one node, and expands one on demand via `/pop`. This repo already has the same shape and the plugin needs no work for it -- the coarse `ct=bubble|backbone` tier with `cn`/`cl` collapse summaries, read through RgfaTabixAdapter, covered by the plugin's bubbleTier.test.ts, and documented under "Level of detail: one node per bubble" in agent-docs/reference/PANGENOME_GRAPHS.md. What is missing is a tier FOR THIS GRAPH, and that file already records why: `gfatools bubble` returns 0 bubbles on a pggb GFA (it needs rGFA SN/SO/SR to place a bubble on a reference), so the pggb tier needs vg snarls or BubbleGun -- which is exactly the tool pangyplot picked. The route is therefore: BubbleGun over the pggb E. coli GFA (vendored at ~/src/vendor/pangyplot/BubbleGun), a converter alongside scripts/bubbles_to_tier_bed.py, upload the segs/links BED pair, and add the track to the hosted demo config -- i.e. two outward-facing steps. Measured what it would buy on the figure: the cut is 53 nodes / 68 edges and most of them are 1 bp alternatives strung along the backbone, so a bubble tier should leave roughly a dozen. Your call on the upload.  BUILT 2026-08-09, and the pggb graph has a bubble tier now. pangenome/pggb_bubble_tier is the new figure: 100 kb around the same IS5 element as 27 nodes, the K12 backbone on rank 0 and eleven bubbles below it, with the element this figure opens arrowed. That is pangyplot's mechanism -- decompose offline, draw the collapsed graph, open one bubble -- and the collapse is what answers "still has many small bubbles": at --min-content 50 every single-base alternative is absorbed into the backbone and only indels survive, so the fine cut's 15 little lenses are simply not drawn while nothing a reader was reading is hidden (each node states its collapsed segment count, traversals, and shortest/longest allele). WHAT UNBLOCKED IT: the plugin needed no work at all -- a collapsed bubble is a reference span with an id and a rank, which is the whole segs/links contract -- and the decomposition was already hosted. `pggb -V` had written ecoli_pggb_snarls.vcf.gz, whose LV=0 records are the top-level bubbles with reference spans, AT traversals and allele sequences, so scripts/snarls_to_bubble_bed.py (new) emits the bubble BED build_bubble_tier.sh already reads. No BubbleGun run and no re-running pggb. Measured: 143,964 top-level snarls, none overlapping, 544 kept at 50, so the whole 4.64 Mb pangenome is 1,088 nodes in 51 kB against 606k fine segments. One real difference from a gfatools bubble file, found by bubbles_to_tier_bed.py's own uniqueness assert rather than by inspection: pggb folds repeats, so one snarl can be reported at two reference loci (67 of 143,897 sources, 134 rows), and the tier id therefore carries the reference start. THIS FIGURE IS UNCHANGED and stays the fine end of the ladder -- it is where the bubble is open. STILL NOT BUILT is popping a bubble open in the app (pangyplot's /pop): that is a second GetSubgraph against the fine prefix spliced into the tier GFA, plus a node menu item, and the design is written down in PANGENOME_GRAPHS.md.
